newsitem.title: USA: Service Corp. says committed to Loewen deal.
newsitem.headline: Service Corp. says committed to Loewen deal.

text.p: Service Corp. International, the nation's largest operator of funeral homes and cemeteries, said Wednesday it remained committed to buying Loewen Group Inc. despite having been rebuffed by its No. 2 rival.
Houston-based Service Corp., which last week offered to buy Loewen in a stock transaction valued at $2.8 billion, said it will hold a board meeting on Oct. 1 to consider its next move.

After meeting for about seven hours to discuss the offer, Loewen's board of directors late Tuesday unanimously rejected the offer, saying the unsolicited $43 per share bid was inadequate and that it intended to remain an independent company.

"We are disappointed that the Loewen board of directors rejected our proposals without ever returning our calls or seeking more information from us. The actions of the Loewen board simply deprive its stockholders of the oppportunity to receive prompt value for their shareholders," Service Corp. Chairman Robert Waltrip said in a news release.

Service Corp. disclosed its offer last week and indicated it would be willing to raise the bid if Loewen granted it access to its financial records. The offer also calls for Service Corp. to assume about $1.3 billion of Loewen debt.
With the rejection, Service Corp. must now decide if it wants to raise the offer or pursue a hostile takeover of Loewen.

Analysts have said that Service might have a difficult time winning Loewen in a hostile bid because Loewen Chief Executive Officer Raymond Loewen holds about 15 percent of the company's common shares and insiders hold about another 3 percent.
A hostile takeover would require the approval of 75 percent of voting Loewen shareholders.
Service Corp. also noted that its offer represented a 48.9 percent premium over the price Loewen stock was trading at 30 days before its offer.

"In addition, since Loewen stockholders would be receiving stock, they would continue to participate in Loewen's business as well as share in the upside of our business," said Service Corp. President William Heiligbrodt.
Shares of Loewen traded on Nasdaq rose 37.5 cents to $41.375. Service Corp. stock edged up 12.5 cents to $30.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
